paper_metadata.title: Microstructural evolution and creep mechanisms in Ni-based single crystal superalloys: A review

evidence.section: Abstract
evidence.quote: Nickel-based single crystal superalloys (Ni-SXs) ar e of great interests in aircraft industry due to their excellent high temperature creep strength deriving from the rigid gamma/gamma prime ( γ/γ′ ) microstructure and the single crystal nature.

evidence.section: 3.3 Rafting mechanism of gamma prime phase

evidence.section: 3.3 Rafting mechanism of gamma prime phase
evidence.quote: The specific coalescence process of γ′ particles is related to a long time hypothesis of elemental transporting through a ‘pipe diffusion’ process with dislocation movements [163].

evidence.section: 3.2 Coarsening mechanism of gamma prime phase
evidence.quote: during the low temperature creep, the creep deformation is mainly caused by the dislocation shearing of γ′ precipitates under high stress.

mechanisms.name: stress concentration at TCP phase interfaces

evidence.quote: large misfit exists between the TCP phase and γ phase that generates high localized stress at the interfaces. At high temperature, stress concentrates on the vicinity of TCP phase which makes it easier for the nucleation of micro-cracks near TCP phases [196].

mechanisms.name: dislocation pile-up at TCP phase boundaries

evidence.quote: TCP phase can act as obstacles against dislocation movements in a slip system. Dislocations pile up at the TCP phase boundaries that cause the strong stress concentration, and then the micro-cracks generate and propagate along the TCP phase according to the movement of dislocations [42, 197]

mechanisms.name: consumption of strengthening elements by TCP phase

evidence.quote: the formation of TCP phase inevitably consumes the strengthening elements and destroys the original regular cross-networks in the vicinity [193].
